facts.statement: Cretorectolobus was an extinct species of carpet shark.
facts.quote: Cretorectolobus is an extinct carpet shark.

facts.statement: The genus Cretorectolobus was first described by G.R. Case in 1978.
facts.quote: It was described by G.R. Case in 1978

facts.statement: Cretorectolobus belongs to the family Orectolobidae.
Cretorectolobus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
Cretorectolobus lived from the Hauterivian to the Maastrichtian, approximately 132.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Maastrichtian (132.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type species, Cretorectolobus olsoni, lived during the Campanian stage in Canada and the United States.
facts.quote: the type species is C. olsoni, which existed during the Campanian in Canada and the United States

facts.statement: The species Cretorectolobus gracilis lived from the Hauterivian to the Barremian in the Speeton Clay Formation of England.
facts.quote: Another species, C. gracilis, was described by Charlie J. Underwood and Mitchell in 1999, from the Hauterivian to Barremian strata of the Speeton Clay Formation of England

facts.statement: The species Cretorectolobus robustus lived during the Cenomanian in Canada.
facts.quote: A new species, C. robustus, was described from the Cenomanian of Canada by Underwood and Stephen L. Cumbaa in 2010

facts.statement: The species name C. gracilis refers to its teeth, which are described as gracile and narrow.
facts.quote: The species epithet refers to the shark's teeth, which Underwood and Mitchell described as gracile and narrow in form

facts.statement: Fossils of Cretorectolobus have been found in the Hauterivian-Barremian Speeton Clay Formation in England.
facts.quote: Fossils of Cretorectolobus have been found in: Hauterivian-Barremian Speeton Clay Formation, England

facts.statement: Fossils of Cretorectolobus have been found in the Albian Cedar Mountain Formation in Utah and in Kolbay, Kazakhstan.
facts.quote: Albian Cedar Mountain Formation, Utah Kolbay, Kazakhstan

facts.statement: Fossils of Cretorectolobus have been found in the Cenomanian of Saskatchewan, Canada.

Fossils of Cretorectolobus have been found in the Campanian Aguja Formation in Mexico, the Dinosaur Park and Judith River Formations in Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Montana, and the Mesaverde Group in Wyoming.
facts.quote: Campanian Aguja Formation, Mexico Dinosaur Park Formation, Alberta Judith River Formation, Saskatchewan, Canada and Montana, United States Mesaverde Group, Wyoming

facts.statement: Fossils of Cretorectolobus have been found in Åsen and Ignaberga, Sweden.
Fossils of Cretorectolobus have been found in the Maastrichtian Kemp Clay Formation in Texas and at Bakla Hill in Ukraine.
facts.quote: Maastrichtian Kemp Clay Formation, Texas Bakla Hill, Ukraine
